The 2000–01 season was Chelsea F.C.'s 87th competitive season, ninth consecutive season in the [[Premier League|FA Premier League]] and 95th year as a club.

==Season summary==
A slow start to the season cost manager [[Gianluca Vialli]] his job, despite having won five trophies since his appointment in February 1998.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vialli sacked as Chelsea boss|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/922110.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=12 September 2000|access-date=3 August 2015}}</ref> The last of these trophies came at the start of the season when they defeated [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] 2–0 in the [[FA Community Shield|Charity Shield]] to win the last-ever club game at the pre-redevelopment Wembley.<ref>{{cite web|title=Keane sees red as Chelsea triumph|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/879061.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=13 August 2000|access-date=3 August 2015}}</ref> Vialli's successor was [[Claudio Ranieri]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Ranieri's Chelsea deal|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/925944.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=15 September 2000|access-date=3 August 2015}}</ref> who guided the club to sixth place in the final table and attained automatic qualification for the [[UEFA Cup]].

The biggest success of the season was the effectiveness of club record signing [[Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink]], who found the net 23 times in 35 Premiership games in a partnership with Chelsea's 34-year-old Italian superstar, [[Gianfranco Zola]], who found the net on 9 occasions.

==Team kit==
The team kit was produced by [[Umbro]] and the shirt sponsor was Autoglass. Chelsea's home kit was all blue with a white trimmed collar. The club's third kit for this season was orange with blue shorts and accents.
